title: Keep zero-length fixed spans in Pipeline9 regional sections
description: Fixes autorouting failure by retaining zero-length fixed spans during regional section assembly, allowing for proper reconstruction of routes in the Pipeline9 autorouter.
body:
## Problem

The exact 96-component T113 fixture contains two identical consecutive fanout points in `fanout:breakout:pcb_breakout_point_68:source-0`. Pipeline9 converts that `1..2` position span into a zero-length fixed route. During the actual `cmn_60` regional fallback, section construction discarded that slice, joined its `0..1` and `2..3` neighbors, and accepted one replacement spanning `0..3`. The stale zero-length identity survived beside its replacement, so reconstruction failed with:

`Pipeline9 could not reconnect mutated preloaded segment "breakout:pcb_breakout_point_68_fixed_168_1"`

## Change

- Retain zero-length fixed slices while contiguous regional sections are assembled, allowing a replacement spanning that position to absorb their source identities.
- Skip a complete assembled section only when the whole section is zero-length, since it has no copper and cannot form a useful fallback port pair.
- Add a deterministic regression using the exact T113 SRJ, trace index 168, actual `cmn_60` bounds and ports, and the accepted replacement captured from the full-board failure.
- Update the exact integration test and PCB SVG with the completed Pipeline9 output.

The exact solver now completes with `solved=true`, `failed=false`, and 42 routed or mutated traces. The resulting board still has downstream routing violations: strict repository DRC reports 69 errors and `tsci check shorts` reports 47 physical shorts. Those require separate reproductions and root fixes.

## Validation

- Focused canonical ownership, zero-length reconstruction, and exact T113 tests: 3 passed, 28 assertions
- Exact 96-component Pipeline9 run: `solved=true`, `failed=false`, `error=null`, 42 routes
- `bun run build`
- `git diff --check`

title: Repro: Pipeline 9 silently narrows requested trace width
description: Reproduces a bug where Pipeline 9 narrows a requested 0.4 mm trace width to 0.2375 mm instead of finding a legal detour, highlighting a flaw in the autorouting logic.
body:
## Repro

Pipeline 9 is asked to route one 0.4 mm trace. The board is 30 × 20 mm, with two unrelated rectangular obstacles near its center. They leave a 0.50 mm shortcut, but 0.4 mm copper plus 0.13 mm clearance on each side needs 0.66 mm. There is over 7 mm of free board space above and below the obstacles; a compliant route is not blocked by the board outline.

With the board-wide minimum at 0.1 mm, Pipeline 9 reports success and chooses the shortcut at 0.2375 mm. The control keeps the **same board, pads, obstacles, endpoints, clearance, and requested 0.4 mm width**; changing only the board-wide minimum to 0.4 mm makes Pipeline 9 find a legal 0.4 mm route around an obstacle, more than 5 mm from the board edge. Thus the router has a feasible full-width path in this geometry. Both panels are generated from actual solver outputs; the gray rectangle shows the board bounds.

![Actual Pipeline 9 output and full-width control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Abse2001/tscircuit-autorouter/codex/repro-pipeline9-trace-width/tests/repro/__snapshots__/pipeline9-silent-trace-width-neckdown.snap.svg)

## Where the width is lost

This reproduces the Game Boy power-path problem: Core converts a TSX trace `thickness="0.4mm"` into `source_trace.min_trace_thickness = 0.4`, then puts it in SRJ as `connection.nominalTraceWidth = 0.4` (`getSimpleRouteJsonFromCircuitJson.ts`). SRJ has only a global `minTraceWidth = 0.1` and no per-connection *minimum*. `TraceWidthSolver` tries nominal, a midpoint, then silently falls back to the board minimum when clearance is insufficient. The resulting board can be geometrically DRC-clean while violating the authored current-carrying width.

The fix should preserve the distinction between a preferred width and a hard per-connection minimum across Core/SRJ/Pipeline 9. The router should take the available compliant detour here; if no compliant route exists, it should report a constraint failure rather than silently narrow the wire. This PR is repro-only, with no solver changes. Related existing issue: #1721.

## Validation

- Focused repro: pass.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: pass.
- `git diff --check`: pass.

## Problem

After the closed-route serialization fix on `main`, Pipeline9 reaches a second ownership mismatch in regional via validation. Generated fixed routes carry canonical `rootConnectionName` values, while board obstacles carry member trace and port IDs. Passing those two forms directly to the generic connectivity API makes the exact T113 route `source_trace_44_fixed_262_13` treat its own `pcb_smtpad_139` as foreign copper.

The full exact run consequently stops at `No path found for source_trace_194` even though the rejected candidate only intersects copper from its own net.

## Change

- Resolve route and obstacle identities to canonical nets at the Pipeline9 regional obstacle-validation boundary.
- Map member IDs before considering an ID as a canonical net key. This preserves the collision case where one string is both a generated net key and a member of another net.
- Keep `circuit-json-to-connectivity-map@0.0.19` and its existing member-ID semantics.
- Add a focused regression that loads the merged, unmodified 96-component T113 fixture and checks the exact same-net pad plus a foreign-net obstacle.
- Update the full exact integration test to prove the solver advances through `source_trace_194` and reaches the next independent reconstruction invariant.

## Visual diff

This PR is stacked on #2592. That PR adds `t113-linux-exact-pipeline9-state.svg` with the exact board and its 342 preloaded traces at the failure boundary. This PR modifies the same file using the same renderer and viewport, adding the 42 routes reached after the canonical ownership fix. body:
The AM3352 DDR routing experiment reaches byte-bus matching, then `LengthMatchingSolver` exhausts its meander search for `DDR_D0`. This PR adds the captured standalone input and an opt-in observed-failure test, with no production solver changes.

The failing comparison is `DDR_D0` (`source_net_70`) against `DDR_D5` (`source_net_87`) with 0.635 mm skew tolerance. The test reproduces `LengthMatchingNoSolutionError`, reason `meander-search-exhausted`, and `required 9.9183mm`.

The fixture was captured at the bus matcher constructor after Pipeline 9's differential-pair stage, using capacity-autorouter 0.0.900 and length-matching-solver commit 96cca6783a6e29d12bb1871185efe6ff2257bef8. It preserves all 48 routes and 908 obstacles and removes only later comparison requests that never run before this failure. Gzip keeps the otherwise 5 MB input to about 189 KB; provenance and decompression instructions are included.

This is a reproduction, not a fix or proof that the requested geometry is feasible. The passing test intentionally confirms today's failure and is opt-in to avoid slowing ordinary CI.

```sh
bun install
RUN_AM3352_DDR_REPRO=1 bun test tests/repros/am3352-ddr-d0.test.ts --timeout 9999999
```

Validation:
- Standalone reproduction: **1 pass, 9 assertions, 178.616 seconds, 59 iterations** (Bun 1.3.2 / macOS arm64).
- Default invocation: **1 skipped, 0 failures**.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run build`, and `bun run typecheck:structure`: passed; structural checks report existing warnings.

title: Fix DDR length matching blocked by unchanged lead clearances
description: Fixes the issue where the DDR_D0 matcher rejected meanders due to unchanged lead clearances, allowing for successful matching while preserving existing terminal leads.
body:
Stacked on #69; review and merge #69 first. This PR targets its reproduction branch.

The captured DDR_D0 matcher rejected meanders because the replacement includes unchanged straight leads beside existing copper/vias. Those inherited lead clearances caused every candidate on useful segments to fail, even when the new meander copper could fit. The solver eventually raised `LengthMatchingNoSolutionError` requesting another 9.9183 mm.

Preserve the clearance state of a replacement segment only when both endpoints lie within one original same-layer segment (1e-9 mm numerical tolerance), and only when the replacement actually introduces new geometry. Newly introduced segments still undergo bounds, obstacle, via, and foreign-trace checks. Plain straight-segment validation retains its existing behavior. No spacing or length tolerance is relaxed, and no failed solve is converted to success.

The #69 fixture now solves and checks DDR_D0/DDR_D5 skew ≤0.635 mm, exact endpoints/vias, and unchanged unrelated routes. A focused geometry test verifies that new copper is still rejected against obstacles, own-net vias, foreign traces, displaced leads, and different-layer geometry. The native final `solver.visualize()` snapshot and PNG are updated to the successful state.

This change does not repair inherited board DRC violations or establish full-board routing/signoff; it validates the copper added by this matching operation.

Validation:
- Captured DDR regression and snapshot verification: **199 assertions, about 26 seconds / 62 iterations** (previously failed after about 179 seconds).
- Focused retained-lead and blind-via tests: **2 passed**.
- Typecheck, build, structural checks: passed; existing structural warnings remain.

Run the captured regression:

```sh
RUN_AM3352_DDR_REPRO=1 bun test tests/repros/am3352-ddr-d0.test.ts --timeout 9999999
```

![Final successful solver visualization](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/length-matching-solver/fix/am3352-preserve-unchanged-leads/fixtures/am3352-ddr-d0/final-visualization.png)

Full-suite result: **83 passed, 1 opt-in test skipped, 1 timing failure**. `rv1106g2-camera-search.test.ts` exceeded its 45-second limit (54.9 seconds in the fix suite). The same test also fails on the unchanged #69 base when run alone (47.6 seconds). This timing limit was not changed or suppressed; the captured DDR regression was run separately and passes. These wall-clock measurements do not establish a performance improvement for the unrelated camera case.

title: Fix Linux processor results and missing TI specification columns
description: Fixes the Linux-capable Processors page by correctly querying TI processor families and mapping DACADC channel specifications, improving data accuracy and availability.
body:
The Linux-capable Processors page was empty because it queried `Arm-based processors`, while TI stores the relevant parts under leaf families such as `Multimedia & industrial networking SoCs`. DAC channel counts were also empty because the mapper did not recognize `Number of DAC channels`.

This change:
- Uses actual TI processor families while retaining per-part Linux/ARM/NPU classification. Preserves explicit CPU metadata and supports additional application processors when TI explicitly declares Linux support and a recognized core.
- Maps DAC/ADC channel aliases, settling time, INL, sample/update rates, regulator dropout/current/noise/PSRR, converter switching frequency/output count, and MCU interfaces/features with unit conversion. Ambiguous package-dependent values and unavailable specifications remain unknown.
- Interleaves missing specifications with remaining basic-information lookups (four specification turns per information turn), prioritizing stocked parts in mapped categories. Keeps the existing 1,500-request daily budget, gateway cooldowns, and update-only catalog behavior.
- Adds D1 indexes for the priority queues and per-family specification coverage in `/api/enrichment/status`.

Read-only production audit: the corrected classifier includes 228 stored Linux-capable processors (185 in stock), and the DAC alias recovers 33 existing channel counts. The broader missing-column issue also reflects incomplete enrichment: 1,652 of 67,549 parts had detailed specifications at audit time; all 1,022 precision DACs and 161 audio DACs were still pending. Those values will fill as the background job fetches TI specifications after its existing budget resets. This PR does not invent values to fill cells or insert new parts.

title: Fix analog switch classification using TI configuration
description: Fixes incorrect classification of analog switches by using TIs configuration metadata to accurately filter and categorize switches and multiplexers.
body:

When configuration is absent, require an explicit analog/bilateral switch description without mux wording. Channel count remains available as a user filter.

The shared filter fixes both JSON and HTML results. Existing Analog Muxes results and endpoint contracts are preserved. This reads existing D1 metadata; no catalog re-import, migration, or additional TI requests are needed. The change takes effect when the updated Worker is deployed.

Ordinary constant-width wire segments can bridge pours; interpolated segments and inferred inline via barrels are conservatively excluded from this fallback. Existing trace checks remain in place.

title: Propose warning_only keepouts and keepout overlap warnings
description: Proposes the Circuit JSON contract for advisory PCB keepouts, allowing routing and copper placement to cross certain keepout regions while reporting overlaps as warnings instead of errors.
body:
Proposes the Circuit JSON contract for advisory PCB keepouts. Today keepouts are enforcing regions and there is no standard keepout-specific warning record. This adds `warning_only?: boolean` to rectangle, circle, and outline keepouts, plus `pcb_keepout_overlap_warning` for overlap diagnostics.

### Proposed semantics

- `warning_only: true`: routing and copper placement may cross the region. DRC producers report overlaps with this keepout as warnings instead of errors.
- Omitted or `false`: preserve normal enforcement. Parsing leaves omitted values absent and rejects non-boolean values.
- `excluded_pcb_component_ids` still applies, including to advisory diagnostics. Other DRC violations and overlaps with enforcing keepouts remain errors.
- The new warning requires a message and `pcb_keepout_id`. Its ID and `warning_type` have standard defaults; optional fields identify affected components, traces, pads, plated holes, vias, overlap center, and subcircuit.

Exports the schema and types and registers the warning in the general parser and PCB element union. Documents the contract and backward compatibility in the README. Parsing does not execute routing or DRC; consumers must implement the behavior, and older consumers may ignore the flag and continue enforcing the region.

### Related work

- Merged JSX prop: https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/854
- Draft core routing implementation: https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4014
- `@tscircuit/checks` warning emission and remaining consumer behavior will follow the agreed standard.

### Validation

All 360 tests pass. Typecheck, Zod lint, snake-case checks, package/declaration build, changed-source formatting, and diff whitespace checks pass. New tests cover all keepout shapes, true/false/omitted values, invalid inputs, exclusions, warning references/defaults, and top-level JSON round-trips.

Proposes `<keepout allowTraces />` and `<keepout allowPlacements />` for rectangular and circular keepouts. A region can permit trace crossings while reserving component space, or permit component placement while remaining a trace obstacle.

Both props are optional booleans. Parsing preserves true, false, and omission without coercion; false or omission grants no permission. The props are independent, have no aliases or conflicting combinations, and require no migration of existing designs.

Allowed overlaps produce no keepout error or warning. `allowPlacements` covers components and their associated pads/plated holes; standalone vias are not exempted. `warningOnly` continues to control advisory behavior for overlaps that remain prohibited. Copper pours still avoid the region with either or both permissions enabled. Existing component exclusions and unrelated design rules remain applicable.

This proposes the public props only; core and checks integration will follow. The accompanying Circuit JSON proposal uses `allow_traces` and `allow_placements`.

The dense MCU breakout fixture uses `autorouterEffortLevel="2x"`: default effort produces a 0.092 mm trace gap with this release, while 2x completes without DRC errors. The SOIC8 fanout PCB snapshot allows 0.005% pixel variation (24 pixels at 800×600). - Final CI on `abf21739`: all 10 test jobs, typecheck, dependency check, formatting, distribution smoke test, and Vercel deployment passed. One job initially hit three intermittent SPICE simulation failures; all three passed locally, and the failed job passed on retry without code or assertion changes.

Regression investigation: the added DATA vias in `manual-breakoutpoints-preserve-plane-fanout` are a confirmed regression introduced in capacity-autorouter 0.0.901 by tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#2514. Joint repair mistakes the phase-local breakout bounds for physical board edges, adds two vias, and leaves the false edge error while creating a real pad-clearance violation. Supplying the actual 12×8 mm board outline with unchanged routing bounds eliminates both added vias. The exact input, release bisect, stage assertions, and visual control are in tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#2649. The earlier assertion change to count only GND vias permits this defect; green CI does not establish that this route is safe. This reproduction does not yet fix the routing regression.

The snapshots preserve those results; this dependency update does not fix those upstream routing issues. Default-effort routing of the dense MCU fixture also remains affected as described above.

The peer dependency remains `*`; core disables lockfile saving. This update supersedes the dependency bump proposed in #3968.

title: Implement warningOnly keepouts with DRC warnings and a TSX example
description: Implements keepout warningOnly  across cores PCB rendering, routing, import, and copper-pour generation, allowing advisory keepouts to emit warnings without blocking autorouting.
body:
Implements `<keepout warningOnly />` across core's PCB rendering, routing, import, and copper-pour generation. Advisory keepouts remain in Circuit JSON for display and DRC, but do not become routing obstacles. Copper pours still avoid both advisory and enforcing keepouts. Normal keepouts retain enforcement. Placement inside an advisory keepout emits a warning without blocking autorouting, and crossing traces produce warnings through the normal board DRC pipeline.

Updates `@tscircuit/props` to `^0.0.661`, `circuit-json` to `^0.0.494` (including overrides), and `@tscircuit/checks` to `^0.0.201`. Uses the canonical `warning_only` field and removes the temporary compatibility type. Imported keepouts retain the flag and layers.

Adds a standalone TSX example at `tests/examples/keepout-warning-only.tsx` and one annotated PCB snapshot. The example shows a pad inside an advisory rectangle, a trace crossing advisory rectangle/circle keepouts, and another trace detouring around an enforcing keepout. The integration test asserts one placement warning, two trace warnings, two completed routes, and no errors.

Validation: nine focused keepout/import/copper-pour/antenna/DRC tests pass, along with TypeScript typecheck, package/declaration build, formatting, and diff whitespace checks. An annotated copper-pour snapshot shows the element code for both keepout types and confirms that each creates a hole in the pour. After restoring this behavior, the copper-pour snapshot, warningOnly routing/DRC test, and existing copper-pour keepout regression all pass. The example snapshot was visually inspected.

Release availability: npm metadata and the publish workflow report checks 0.0.201, but its tarball currently returns HTTP 404. Local validation used the built implementation from the merged checks PR. Keep this draft until the published package can be installed and CI confirms the dependency update.

Related merged PRs: https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/854, https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/803, https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/pull/304.

title: Support board default via tenting with per-via overrides
description: Adds support for board default via tenting with per-via overrides, allowing vias to inherit board settings unless explicitly overridden, and updates related tests and dependencies.
body:
`<board defaultViaTenting>` stores per-side defaults on `pcb_board`. Vias leave tenting undefined unless explicitly overridden, so `<via tented={false}>` stays exposed while unspecified vias inherit their board's settings.

Preserves imported board defaults and route-via overrides, including `false`, and flips explicit sides with the footprint. Boards include their subcircuit ID so renderers resolve the correct defaults in panels. Updates `circuit-to-svg` to `^0.0.424`.

Adds two focused tests: a labelled panel snapshot for opposite board defaults and explicit via overrides, and a stitching snapshot verifying generated vias inherit the board default. Existing route-import coverage checks explicit tenting alongside via dimensions; two existing board JSON snapshots include the new fields.

Validation: both new tests and the three existing via/import regression tests pass. Related to #3903.

title: Fix bus constraints for traces connected through named nets
description: Fixes autorouting failure for traces connected through named nets by resolving bus members connections accurately and supporting named nets without merging distinct branches.
body:
Enabling the DDR bus constraints in `seveibar/am3352-dev-board` stopped routing with `Could not find an SRJ connection for ".U1 > .M3" in bus "DDR_BYTE0"`. Its pins connect through named nets, whose autorouter connections are named by source net ID and have no `source_trace_id`.

Resolve each bus member by its exact source trace first. When no direct routing connection exists, fall back to its subcircuit connectivity group and connected net IDs. This supports named nets without merging distinct branches that share an electrical net. Existing missing/duplicate connection errors remain in place.

Adds an end-to-end named-net bus regression with a single-scenario PCB snapshot showing TSX, 20 mm/24 mm routes, and the actual 4 mm skew error against a 2 mm limit. Eight regression tests pass, including the shared-capacitor and SII9022 HDMI fanout tests that failed in CI. Typecheck passes; the initial package build also passed.

Verified by rebuilding `seveibar/am3352-dev-board` with its previously unused `TimingConstraints` component enabled. The rebuild emits both source buses and preserves all 2,453 saved trace routes exactly. It has no bus-skew errors or routing failures; its only errors are the two existing crystal-net maximum-length violations. All 11 of the board’s separate planar DDR checks pass.

![Named-net bus length regression](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/8da991966215e262e1ff24dd8eabe7a04dea687c/tests/components/primitive-components/bus/__snapshots__/net-connections-pcb.snap.svg)

title: Integrate routed trace and bus length DRC checks
description: Integrates routed trace and bus length DRC checks by updating the checks library and implementing new error handling for trace lengths and bus skew violations.
body:
Bump `@tscircuit/checks` to `^0.0.200` so the existing routing DRC pipeline emits `pcb_trace_too_long_error` and `pcb_bus_length_skew_error` after `renderUntilSettled()`. A 30 mm trace with `maxLength="24mm"` now produces an error; a bus with 20 mm and 30 mm routes and `maxLengthSkew="2mm"` reports 10 mm skew.

Skip bus members already preserved as routed copper when constructing pending autorouter connections. This prevents an SRJ lookup error for manually routed bus traces while retaining all members in `source_bus` for length checking.

Four end-to-end tests cover board trace length, board bus skew, standalone subcircuit length, and the platform `routingDrcChecksDisabled` setting. Each snapshot contains one scenario with native, left-aligned multiline `pcbnotetext`, TSX, measured lengths, and the actual emitted error where applicable. Repeated rendering is checked for duplicate errors.

title: Fix floating JST housing by honoring Rotate angles in vanilla renderer
description: Fixes the floating issue of the JST housing by correctly applying rotation angles in the vanilla renderer, ensuring proper positioning of the housing and pins.
body:
The vanilla renderer ignores the `angles` prop used by `<Rotate>` in the JST-PH model. As a result, the housing is translated upward without its preceding 180° flip and floats 6 mm above its intended mounting plane. Both 3d-viewer and circuit-json-to-gltf consume this vanilla model generator.

Read `angles` before the existing `rotation` alias, preserving the per-axis fallback and angle conversion. This fixes the housing without shifting the correctly positioned pins.

The same fix restores rotations on rectangular footprint pads. Update the three affected snapshots (JST-SH, SOT143, and slide switch) and verify their pad bounds against the footprint data. Existing JST-PH snapshots use React/jscad-fiber, so add a full-model vanilla regression to cover the path used by the viewer and exporter.

Validation:
- All 272 tests pass locally (4,872 assertions).
- Regression tests cover `angles`, the `rotation` alias, and axis props with degree strings.
- Full vanilla JST-PH model: housing Z bounds are 0–6 mm; pin bounds remain −3.4–5.5 mm.
- Geometry checks confirm the rotated pad dimensions and centers for all three updated snapshots.
- Build, TypeScript checking, changed-file formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.

title: Honor allow_traces and allow_placements keepout permissions
description: Honors allow_traces and allow_placements on keepouts, allowing traces and padsplated holes to emit neither errors nor warnings while keeping vias checked and applying warning_only to prohibited overlaps.
body:
Honors `allow_traces` and `allow_placements` on keepouts. Allowed traces and pads/plated holes emit neither errors nor warnings; vias remain checked, and `warning_only` still applies to prohibited overlaps.

Updates Circuit JSON to 0.0.495 and adds one annotated visual test showing each permission independently and together. No README changes.

Follows https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/805 and https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/855.

title: Fix do-not-place mixed courtyard overlaps
description: Fixes courtyard overlap checks for do-not-place components to ensure proper collision detection without suppressing copper collisions.
body:
Follow-up to #291.

`checkCourtyardOverlap` already ignores courtyards owned by `do_not_place` components, but `checkPcbComponentOverlap` independently reports courtyard-to-plated-hole collisions. Skip only courtyard-involving comparisons when either component is do-not-place, while preserving copper-to-copper overlap checks.

Regression coverage now uses TSX and includes:
- the real SparkFun FS3000-1005 optional JP4/JP5 header geometry
- the full generated circuit JSON as checker input plus PCB SVG snapshots
- a separate plated-hole overlap safeguard proving do-not-place does not suppress copper collisions

Verified with:
- `bun run build`
- `bun test`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`

title: Emit warnings for warning_only keepout violations
description: A keepout with warning_only: true now produces pcb_keepout_overlap_warning diagnostics instead of placement or trace errors.
body:
A keepout with `warning_only: true` now produces `pcb_keepout_overlap_warning` diagnostics instead of placement or trace errors. This implements the standard merged in https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/803 and updates the development dependency to `circuit-json ^0.0.494`.

`checkPcbCopperOverKeepout` emits warnings for pads, plated holes, and vias, retaining all affected copper IDs when grouping multiple contacts by component/keepout. `checkEachPcbTraceNonOverlapping` emits one warning per trace/keepout even when several trace segments violate the region. Aggregate runners preserve both kinds of warnings.

False/omitted flags retain existing errors. Layer filtering, component and connected-trace exclusions, existing geometry checks, and unrelated DRC errors retain their behavior. The return types now include the warning type, and existing error-specific test consumers narrow by `type` before accessing error-specific fields. Adds repository guidance that new features do not automatically warrant a README section.

Adds one demonstrative visual snapshot comparing identical pad and trace overlaps in advisory and enforcing keepouts. `pcbnotetext` annotations show the relevant element code and the diagnostic types returned by the checks.

Validation: all 372 tests and TypeScript typecheck pass; package/declaration build passed for the unchanged implementation. Changed-source formatting and diff whitespace checks pass. The snapshot was visually inspected.

Related core implementation: https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4014

title: Report bus skew and trace length violations as routing errors
description: Enforces bus length-skew requirements and maximum-length violations as routing errors, enhancing the routing error reporting mechanism.
body:
Bus length-skew requirements currently produce no routing errors, and individual `max_length` violations only produce warnings. Enforce both using the schemas added in https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/798.

- Add `checkPcbBusLengthSkew` to the public API and routing/all-check pipelines. Compare the longest and shortest routed members of each `source_bus`, returning measured skew and affected trace IDs.
- Return `pcb_trace_too_long_error` for trace maximum-length violations. Sum PCB route fragments per source trace while preserving exact-endpoint filtering for unrelated branches.
- Share fallback route measurement and fix skipped via-to-wire distances and through-pad traversal. Prefer router-provided lengths; retain the existing 1.6mm fallback per via.
- Require `circuit-json ^0.0.493` and change maximum-length findings from warnings to errors. Unrouted bus members remain the responsibility of connectivity checks.

Companion core PR: https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3992

Tests cover inclusive limits, zero skew, numerical boundary noise, fragment totals, unrouted members, branch attribution, subcircuit isolation, and routing-pipeline integration.

Validation against published dependencies after rebasing onto main: 371 tests pass. Build, TypeScript, formatting, and dependency policy pass locally. CI is rerunning for the visual-test update.

Each snapshot is a single failing PCB rendered directly by circuit-to-svg. All annotations are native TSX `pcbnotetext`: the actual TSX declaration (including the trace path), route segment lengths, arithmetic showing why the constraint failed, and the actual DRC message in red. The tests assert that adding annotations leaves the returned error unchanged. There are no comparison panels or custom SVG layouts.

The bus fixture shows 20mm and 30mm members exceeding a 2mm skew limit. The trace fixture shows a 5 + 20 + 5mm detour exceeding its 24mm maximum. Source requirements and copper routes come from TSX, with no synthetic source buses or trace-length overrides.

title: Repair native high-density nodes before stitching
description: Repairs copper-clearance violations inside native high-density nodes before stitching, ensuring compliance with minimum trace width and connectivity requirements.
body:
Repair actual copper-clearance violations inside every native high-density node before stitching. Pipeline4/7/8/9 pass the board's minimum trace width and connectivity into repair02, and the old node-count cutoff stays removed. The per-node inputs include immutable nearby copper and net/layer-aware pads, so repair does not depend on the order in which other nodes finish.

The previous implementation could approve moves using 0.10 mm node traces even when the board required 0.15 mm copper. It also forced DRC-clean traces away from node boundaries, failed to move free interior corners next to fixed ports, and grouped separate via contacts together. Repair02 now handles these cases directly, budgets work by conflict count, and avoids repeated conflict-key and frame-stat computation. Boundary proximity alone no longer triggers a redraw. No new repair03 calls or bounded-board reconstruction are introduced.

Validation:
- Repair02 PR https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair02/pull/71: 92 tests and CI green.
- The previously regressing SRJ20 sample169, bugreport88, and Pipeline9 bugreport94 finish with zero reference DRC errors. The large boards also pass on Linux. The small BGA case now uses 34 vias versus 33.
- On bugreport94, independently checking the same native input before and after node repair reduces pre-downstream reference DRC errors from 215 to 173. The remaining three new error IDs are existing accidental contacts becoming positive-clearance violations, not new contacts.
- Regression coverage verifies all 81 nodes are processed, physical minimum trace width, fixed node ports, unchanged neighboring copper, separate via contacts, and rounded through-hole boundaries.
- All nine autorouter integration shards, type checking, formatting, and production/preview builds pass on `a7bb956`: https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/35412957566. Updated routing snapshots for the final revision. Sample 4 remains DRC-clean and within the unchanged region/candidate/search-node limits; its reference-validation expectation changes from 9 to 11 (main used 6).

Final dataset18 same-machine benchmark on `268a3fa` against main `8fae1e7`: https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/35411493269.

| Metric | Main | PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Completed / DRC-clean | 13/16 | 13/16 |
| Timeouts | 1 | 1 |
| P50 | 88.8s | 85.5s (-3.6%) |
| P90 | 241.8s | 234.8s (-2.9%) |
| Matched completed boards: global + joint DRC | 360.9s | 293.6s (-18.6%) |
| Matched completed boards: native node repair | 0.006s | 64.7s |

The serial-stage benefit comes from joint repair (306.4s → 238.0s); global repair alone changed from 54.5s to 55.6s. No solved/failed outcomes regressed. Sample 4's total time improved 118.3s → 116.2s despite two additional reference checks versus the earlier PR expectation. These are measured non-networked results, not an estimate of warm-cache networked performance.

title: fix: update jscad-electronics to 0.0.178 for corrected JST housing
description: Fixes incorrect orientation of JST PH housing in 3D exports by updating jscad-electronics to version 0.0.178, which includes a fix for the rendering issue.
body:
## Why

3D exports using the `jst2_p2mm_ph` footprint (for example, a two-pin `J_BAT` connector) can show a floating, incorrectly oriented JST PH housing. The upstream vanilla renderer ignored the `angles` prop on `Rotate`, so the housing's 180° rotation was skipped while its translation was still applied. This left the housing above the board with its opening facing the wrong direction.

[jscad-electronics#388](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/pull/388) fixes this by honoring `Rotate angles`, seating the housing at the board surface with its opening facing upward. The published `0.0.178` package includes that fix.

## Change

Update `jscad-electronics` from `^0.0.159` to `^0.0.178`. These pre-1.0 caret ranges do not overlap, so the existing dependency range cannot pick up the fixed release. This lets circuit-json-to-gltf consume the corrected geometry without adding a workaround to its own transforms.

Only `package.json` changes; this repository does not track its Bun lockfile.

## Validation

- `bun install` resolves `jscad-electronics@0.0.178`.
- `bun run build` passes.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` passes.
- `bunx biome format package.json` and `git diff --check` pass.
- `bun test tests/`: 126 passed, 1 failed. The existing `repro8-scale: board with ~880 plated holes` stress test exceeded its 100,000 ms timeout. All other tests passed; no snapshots were rebaselined. Whether this timeout is caused by the dependency update has not been established.
- The originating J_BAT reproduction was re-rendered after rebuilding jscad-electronics and visually checked; its rotation and JST PH snapshot tests passed (5 tests).

Altium pad records can store layer-specific `ROUNDRECT` geometry and two independent plated-slot dimensions. ## Summary

Add diagnostic Storybook stories and browser comparisons of the actual `3d-viewer` against GLBs generated by pinned, development-only `circuit-json-to-gltf@0.0.129`.

**This PR changes neither production renderer.** There are no changes under `src/` or `lib/`, no renderer corrections hidden in the harness, and no approved screenshot baselines. Existing differences deliberately remain visible as failing, non-blocking diagnostics.

## What reviewers can see

Run `bun run storybook:comparisons` to open **Diagnostics / Renderer Parity / X Rotation** directly. Each story automatically shows both oblique and side comparisons: the normal rendered boards, unlit component geometry, edge maps, red/cyan overlay, and downloadable PNGs with camera metadata and metrics. Bottom-layer stories look from below.

The inputs isolate X/Y signs, mixed-axis order, missing and explicit nonzero origins, implicit bottom-layer orientation, and binary GLB dispatch through `gltfUrl`. Oblique angle probes avoid quarter-turn symmetries. Explicit-origin zero/Z cases are controls.

The USB mounting example uses the measured native Z-up model with rotation `(0,0,270)`, an explicit datum and common reference board. Only that fixture's two pill slots are rotated 90 degrees to accept the metal tabs. A geometry test checks all four tabs against the apertures and all five contacts against the pads. The captured input is preserved, and its original missing-origin case remains a separate diagnostic.

## Comparison contract

- Identical local model bytes and Circuit JSON feed both real rendering paths; models are not fetched from ModelCDN during tests.
- Only the fixed final GLB-to-project coordinate basis is normalized. No registration, recentering, rescaling, or pose correction is allowed.
- Component-only captures preserve loaded world transforms and use shared 640x640 orthographic cameras, white unlit double-sided surfaces, black backgrounds, and depth-tested crease lines.
- The same pure matcher runs in the browser UI and tests: bidirectional Euclidean edge coverage, 1.5 px tolerance, at most 1% unmatched edges independently on either side. Empty or clipped captures fail.
- Viewer-only calibration accepts identical copies and rejects deliberate sign, Euler-order and 0.2248885 mm translation defects. It does not load an exported GLB.

## CI and local results

GitHub Actions installs matching Chromium/Linux libraries and uses Node 22, Bun 1.3.14 and software WebGL. Matcher/unit tests and calibration are blocking. Actual renderer comparisons retain ordinary failed assertions, reports, images and traces but are intentionally non-blocking. Missing/malformed reports and runner failures still produce errors from the diagnostic wrapper; the workflow marks only the diagnostic step `continue-on-error`.

Vercel continues to host Storybook, not run the browser suite. `build-storybook` now prepares the local comparison assets, so the existing `vercel-build` entry point includes working stories.

title: Preserve Altium PCB net connectivity
description: Preserves Altium PCB net identities by creating Circuit JSON source nets and traces for every Altium net, linking routed tracks and arcs to their source trace, and retaining copper-pour net ownership.
body:
PCB conversion previously discarded Altium net identity, leaving traces, vias, and copper pours electrically anonymous even when the source board contained explicit nets. Motive: Keep imported boards electrically usable for net-aware inspection, editing, and design-rule workflows.

title: fix: respect rounded SMT pad corners in copper clearance checks
description: Fixes the copper clearance checks for rounded rectangular SMT pads by accurately measuring against their actual geometry, correcting a bug that misreported clearance gaps.
body:
Rounded rectangular SMT pads currently use their sharp rectangular bounds for copper clearance. A 2×2 mm pad with 0.5 mm corners and a nearby 0.2 mm obstacle can therefore report a 0.324 mm gap where the actual gap is 0.531 mm, incorrectly violating a 0.5 mm rule.

This fixes the shared pad, trace, and via clearance geometry by measuring against an inset rectangle and subtracting the corner radius. Rotation is preserved; fully rounded rectangles use pill geometry to avoid degenerate polygons. Trace/via error markers use the actual copper edges. Sharp rectangular pads retain their existing behavior.

Fixes the rounded-pad clearance bug reproduced in #315 (merged). This PR targets `main`.

- Converts the six separate rounded-corner reproduction files from `test.failing` to ordinary tests, retaining their SVG snapshots.
- Adds explicit geometry tests for two rounded pads, maximum and oversized radii, rotated fully rounded pads, overlap, and marker placement.
- Validation: `bun test` — 405 pass, 0 fail; `bunx --no-install tsc --noEmit` passes; Biome formatting passes for changed files.

title: test: reproduce rounded-pad clearance false positives
description: Reproduces false clearance violations for rounded rectangular SMT pads through comprehensive tests, documenting the behavior of existing bugs in clearance checks.
body:
Rounded rectangular SMT pads produce false clearance violations near their corners because the shared pad-clearance geometry treats them as sharp rectangles. This test-only PR reproduces the behavior through `checkPadTraceClearance`, `checkPadPadClearance`, and `checkViaPadClearance`, with both 0° and 37° pad rotations.

For a 2 × 2 mm pad with a 0.5 mm corner radius, a trace endpoint/circular pad/via centered at local (1.3, 1.3) with 0.1 mm copper radius has an actual gap of `sqrt(2) * 0.8 - 0.5 - 0.1 ≈ 0.53137 mm`. It should pass a 0.5 mm minimum. Current checks instead use the sharp corner and report approximately 0.32426 mm.

The six reproduction cases assert the correct behavior and use `test.failing` to document the known bug on current main (`c2d196b`, v0.0.203). Twelve ordinary control tests move the obstacle closer or remove the rounding to ensure actual clearance violations remain detected. Explicit clearance options isolate the geometry bug from board defaults, and all fixture elements are separate copper groups.

Validation:

- `bun test tests/lib/*rounded-corner-*.test.ts`: **24 passes, 0 failures (including 6 `test.failing` reproductions and 6 snapshot tests)**.
- Existing pad-to-trace, pad-to-pad, and via-to-pad clearance test files: **10 passes**.
- `bunx --no-install tsc --noEmit`: passed.
- Biome formatting and `git diff --check`: passed.

No implementation or dependency changes. The reproductions use `test.failing`, so the test run passes while the bug exists and alerts maintainers when the assertions start succeeding.


Six PCB SVG snapshots cover each clearance check at 0° and 37°. They render the legal rounded-corner geometry on the top layer without recording the incorrect DRC markers as an expected baseline. Snapshot tests run separately from the `test.failing` reproduction assertions.


Each of the six check/rotation cases now has its own self-contained test file with explicit snapshot, legal-gap, closer-obstacle, and sharp-corner tests. There are no loops or parameterized test generators.

SRJ18's large boards failed routing or exhausted the CI timeout. This change bounds routing work and adds validated congestion repair. The exact `/benchmark --dataset 18` run on green commit `9032401` now reports **87.5% completion and 87.5% relaxed DRC pass** (14/16 for both), with the original 360-second timeout and eight-worker concurrency.

Reject physically overlapping unrelated terminals before exhausting an infeasible intra-node portfolio.
- Bound multilayer grid and regional repair work. Use coarse-to-fine weighted regional search with shared node limits and reserved candidate calls for remaining conflicts. Reserve all board layers for ordinary drilled vias and merge only reported same-net via conflicts. Validate complete proposals against reference DRC and physical copper guards before publishing them.

Dependencies: [high-density-repair03 #142](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/142), [repair04 #16](https://github.com/tscircuit/repair04/pull/16), and [tiny-hypergraph #207](https://github.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/pull/207), pinned to tested commits.

The [exact benchmark command](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2662#issuecomment-5750646721) produced this [CI benchmark result](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2662#issuecomment-5750649855):

| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Completion | 81.3% | **87.5%** |
| Relaxed DRC pass | 56.3% | **87.5%** |

The raw report confirms sample 14 completes with zero DRC errors in **299.363 seconds**, below the unchanged 360-second limit. Sample 6 retains its routing failure and sample 15 still times out. description: Fixes the transformation order of rotated and mirrored symbols in KiCad export, ensuring correct graphic and port directions.

## Motivation

KiCad rotates placed symbol geometry before applying the instance mirror. The converter composed those operations in the opposite order, so symbols combining rotation and mirroring could face the wrong direction. ## Changes

title: Render layer-specific keepout arcs distinctly
description: Render layer-specific keepout arcs with a distinct color and metadata in PCB SVG output to prevent confusion with conductive traces.
body:
## Summary

- mark arcs with `KEEPOUT=true` using `data-keepout="true"` in PCB SVG output
- render layer-specific keepout arcs with the established Keepout layer color instead of their copper-layer color
- add focused assertions and an SVG snapshot comparing ordinary copper and keepout arcs

## Why this is needed

A keepout arc can be assigned to a copper layer, but it does not represent conductive copper. It defines a boundary where routing, copper, vias, or component placement is prohibited.

The renderer previously ignored `KEEPOUT=true` and painted these arcs exactly like ordinary copper on the same layer. That makes PCB previews misleading: reviewers can mistake a restriction boundary for a conductive trace, and downstream SVG consumers have no way to identify the geometry as a keepout.

TI PMP22650 exposes the issue clearly because it contains 175 keepout arcs across copper layers. Giving these arcs the established Keepout color and `data-keepout="true"` metadata makes the visual distinction explicit while preserving their original layer assignment.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/svg/pcb-keepout-arc.test.ts tests/svg/pcb-layer-paint-order.test.ts`
